beats.label: hook
beats.text: They knocked on doors. They asked for your DNA. Then they billed Medicare 522 million dollars.

beats.label: setup
beats.text: Reyad Salahaldeen, 57, of Buford Georgia, controlled four laboratories across New Jersey, Georgia, and Texas. From 2018 to 2020, he paid kickbacks to a network of marketers.

beats.label: escalation
beats.text: They harvested DNA from elderly Americans through telemarketing, door-to-door solicitation, and health fairs. The DNA was for expensive genetic tests. To make them billable, Salahaldeen paid doctors and nurse practitioners for signed orders. Doctors who had never treated the patients.

beats.label: resolution
beats.text: When federal agents came with an arrest warrant, Salahaldeen drove from North Carolina to Texas and tried to cross into Mexico using another person's identification. He was caught at the border. 522 million billed. 84 million actually paid. This month: 151 months in federal prison. 11 co-conspirators have already pleaded guilty.

spoken_text: They knocked on doors. They asked for your DNA. Then they billed Medicare 522 million dollars. To make them billable, Salahaldeen paid doctors and nurse practitioners for signed orders. Doctors who had never treated the patients. When federal agents came with an arrest warrant, Salahaldeen drove from North Carolina to Texas and tried to cross into Mexico using another person's identification. He was caught at the border. 522 million billed. 84 million actually paid. This month: 151 months in federal prison. 11 co-conspirators have already pleaded guilty.
